breath_title: Keep the human in the loop.
breath_text: The APA Education Committee hand-sifted 2,996 abstracts to name the 11 must-read med ed papers of 2025. Meanwhile, most IM clerkships still have no clear AI policy, a medical school study finds that early struggles predict later ones (and need more than academic fixes), and a new essay asks how we grow after we get it wrong.

coffee.title: Coffee break with Beth
coffee.note: In my own words. Written by Beth, not AI.
paragraphs: This week is a short one since I'm on service - just a note to amplify the work by the indomitable Gayatri Madduri and team on top articles in Peds Med Ed. 2,996 abstracts, 120 full text articles, 11 selected. Wow wow! And for what it's worth in this age of AI, I very much stand behind the importance of human touch in doing this onerous review to describe and shape our field.

top.headline: Your 2025 med ed reading list, curated by humans: 11 papers out of 2,996
bullets: APA Education Committee members screened 18 journals with blinded, standardized scoring of 2,996 abstracts, then read 120 full texts.
Consensus picked 11 Top Articles in 6 domains: CBME assessment for residents, CBME assessment for fellows, metrics, wellness, anti-racism, and belonging.
Common threads: standardizing assessment (e.g., EPAs), promoting belonging, and supporting trainee retention and well-being.
top.tip: make it a journal club series: one domain per month gets you through the list by spring. Open access.
top.citation: Congdon M, Madduri GB, Frohna JG, Han P, Li ST, Lyle ANJ, Roth LT, Seelbach EB. Acad Pediatr. Online Nov 4, 2026. doi:10.1016/j.acap.2026.103731

top.headline: Is AI cheating? Most clerkship directors aren't sure what the rules are
bullets: National survey of IM clerkship directors (Sep-Dec 2024): 114/141 schools responded (80.9%).
39.5% reported no formal AI policy and 34.2% didn't know if one existed. AI on a reflection essay was "cheating" to 42.9% vs 5.2% for clinical diagnosis.
73.7% would encourage AI for at least one clinical skill, but only 6.1% said their institution offers firewall-protected AI tools.
top.tip: residents supervise these students. Agree on a unit-level AI norm (what's OK, what needs disclosure) before students guess.
top.citation: McQuade CN, Kumar NL, Schaye V, Olson APJ, Hufmeyer KK, McBee E, Kisielewski M, Osman NY, Bonifacino E. Acad Med. Online Nov 5, 2026. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag350

top.headline: Remediation once, risk again: what 758 medical students teach us
bullets: Five cohorts (matriculated 2014-2018): 146/758 (19.3%) needed at least one pre-clinical block remediation; 81 remediated 2-5 blocks.
No exam-trend pattern flagged who would struggle, but prior remediation raised the odds of future block struggles.
Any remediation was tied to extra Step 1 study time and more first-attempt Step 1 failures; the number of remediations was not.
top.tip: a struggle is a signal, not a sentence. Pair academic plans with social and well-being support, and most learners go on to thrive.
top.citation: Anstey JE, Haedinger LA, Philipp TC, Schneider BN, Albright A, Carney PA, Pope BA. Med Teach. Online Nov 3, 2026. doi:10.1080/0142159X.2026.2749548

acadpeds.text: My Life, My Story, for kids. Duke adapted the VA life-story program: 34 inpatients and caregivers; 6 themes (e.g., "What makes me 'me'") that could enrich social histories.
acadpeds.authors: Ayyappan M, ... Loriaux AB. Online Nov 4, 2026.

acadpeds.text: Does MH training change practice? 425 REACH-trained clinicians vs 537 matched peers: more MH services and prescribing, but no change in psychotherapy or ED visits.
acadpeds.authors: Gilbert JL, ... Krist AH. Online Nov 3, 2026.

quick.text: Error, failure, fallibility. A Theory Matters piece separates the event, the judgment, and the human condition, and proposes "fallibility integration" in professional identity formation (Adkins S, Andarsio E. Adv Health Sci Educ. Online Nov 3, 2026).
Can reading build empathy? Meta-analysis of 14 studies (1,593 people): SMD 0.83 for literary-arts interventions, but I2 96% and low-quality evidence (Winter R et al. Med Teach. Online Nov 4, 2026).
Changing a curriculum? Scoping review: 21 studies, 17 change models (Kotter's 8 steps most common); none fit every setting (Arooj M et al. Med Teach. Online Nov 5, 2026).
Two-Eyed Seeing PhD. UND's Indigenous Health PhD: 87 students in 7 cohorts, 32 graduates, only 4 left (Schroeder S, Nadeau M. Acad Med. Online Nov 5, 2026).
